items.title: Satellite images show smoke over Dubai as Iran's Gulf strikes enter third day

featured_image.name: Satellite images show smoke rising over Dubai after Iranian ...

items.description: Satellite imagery captured on March 1 has revealed thick plumes of black smoke rising over Dubai's skyline, offering stark visual evidence of the damage caused by Iran's ongoing retaliatory missile and drone attacks across the Persian Gulf region. The before-and-after images — comparing clear skies on February 24 with smoke columns and burn marks days later — underscore how quickly the conflict between the United States and Iran has reached the doorstep of the Gulf's most prominent commercial hub.[1][2]

items.title: AWS outage spreads to Bahrain as Gulf strikes continue

featured_image.name: Amazon's Cloud Service AWS Hit With Iranian Missile In UAE ...

items.description:
Amazon Web Services suffered a major disruption to its cloud infrastructure in the United Arab Emirates after unidentified objects struck one of its data centers on Sunday, sparking a fire that forced an extended power shutdown as Iranian retaliatory strikes battered the Gulf region.

AWS confirmed on its status page that at approximately 4:30 a.m. PST on March 1, its Availability Zone mec1-az2 in the ME-CENTRAL-1 Region "was impacted by objects that struck the data center, creating sparks and fire". The fire department cut power to the entire facility, including backup generators, while crews worked to extinguish the blaze. The company did not confirm or deny whether the incident was connected to the Iranian strikes when asked by Reuters.[1][2][3][4][5]

items.title: Iran's top security chief rejects talks with US as strikes enter third day

featured_image.name: Ali Larijani appointed as secretary of Iran's Supreme ...

items.description:
Ali Larijani, the head of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, declared on Monday that Tehran "will not negotiate with the United States," flatly rejecting claims that Iranian officials had sought to restart talks with Washington. The statement, posted on X, came hours after President Donald Trump told The Atlantic that Iran's new leadership wanted dialogue and that he had "agreed to talk".[1][2][3][4]

Larijani's rebuke marks a sharp public break with the diplomatic track Trump floated over the weekend, even as US and Israeli strikes on Iran entered their third day following the killing of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei on Saturday.[5][6]

items.title: Israel strikes Beirut after Hezbollah shatters ceasefire with rocket attack

featured_image.name: Israel strikes Beirut for the first time since a ceasefire ...

items.description:
Israel launched its most intensive airstrikes on Beirut since the 2024 war early Monday, pounding Hezbollah-controlled southern suburbs of the Lebanese capital after the Iran-backed group fired rockets and drones at northern Israel for the first time since a U.S.-brokered ceasefire took effect in November 2024. More than a dozen explosions rocked Beirut beginning around 2:40 a.m. local time, sending residents fleeing on foot and by car and clogging roads out of the city.[1][2]

The exchange marks a dramatic widening of the conflict that erupted over the weekend when the United States and Israel launched strikes on Iran, killing Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.[3][4]

items.title: Iran fires missiles at Israel and US sites across Gulf in retaliation

featured_image.name: Israel strikes Beirut suburb targeting Hezbollah drone depot ...

items.description:
Iran launched a sweeping wave of missile and drone attacks against Israel and U.S. military installations across the Persian Gulf over the weekend, striking targets in at least eight countries in retaliation for a joint U.S.-Israeli military operation that killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei on Saturday.

The Iranian offensive, which began hours after coordinated American and Israeli strikes hit Tehran and other Iranian cities on February 28, has killed at least nine Israelis in a single ballistic missile strike on Beit Shemesh, three U.S. service members, and several others across the Gulf region, while injuring hundreds and paralyzing air travel across the Middle East.

items.title: Factory growth accelerates across Indonesia, India, Thailand in February

featured_image.name: Indonesia's manufacturing activity hits 11-month high ahead ...

items.description: Factory activity across three of Southeast and South Asia's largest economies gained momentum in February, with purchasing managers' index data released Monday by S&P Global showing accelerating expansion in Indonesia, India, and Thailand, driven by strengthening domestic demand and rising new orders.

items.title: Melania Trump to chair UN Security Council amid US war on Iran

featured_image.name: Melania Trump set to make history at UN Security Council meeting

items.description:
First Lady Melania Trump is scheduled to preside over a United Nations Security Council meeting on Monday afternoon, an unprecedented appearance that was planned weeks ago but now collides with the reality of active US military operations in Iran.

The session, titled "Children, Technology, and Education in Conflict," will mark the first time a sitting US First Lady has chaired the 15-member council, according to UN spokesperson Stephane Dujarric. The meeting comes as the United States assumes the rotating presidency of the Security Council for March.[1][2][3]

items.title: BOJ deputy governor says rate hikes to continue

featured_image.name: Bank of Japan deputy governor says rate hikes likely to ...

items.description:
Bank of Japan Deputy Governor Ryozo Himino said Monday that the central bank should continue raising interest rates as it moves toward a more neutral monetary policy, reinforcing expectations that further tightening lies ahead even as the Japanese economy sends mixed signals.

"While the Bank's policy remains somewhat accommodative, it should gradually shift to a more neutral stance through moderate policy rate hikes," Himino said in a speech to local business leaders in Wakayama.[1][2]

items.title: Canada's Carney arrives in Delhi for Modi talks amid Iran crisis

featured_image.name: PM Carney lands in New Delhi, plans to meet Modi tomorrow

items.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney landed in New Delhi on Saturday as part of a three-nation tour aimed at deepening trade ties with Indo-Pacific partners, even as U.S.-Israeli military strikes on Iran and Tehran's retaliatory attacks across the Middle East cast a shadow over global diplomacy.

items.title: Trump confirms three US troops killed as he warns more may follow

featured_image.name: Trump Warns More U.S. Casualties Are Possible in Iran Operation

items.description:
President Donald Trump acknowledged Sunday that three American service members had been killed during the U.S.-Israeli military offensive against Iran and warned that more casualties were likely as combat operations continue. "We have three casualties, but we expect more; ultimately, this will lead to a significant outcome for the world," Trump told NBC News.[1]

The deaths, announced by U.S. Central Command at 9:30 a.m. ET on March 1, mark the first confirmed American fatalities since the joint operation — dubbed Operation Epic Fury — began early Saturday. Five additional service members were seriously wounded, while several others sustained minor shrapnel injuries and concussions and were returning to duty, CENTCOM said in a post on X.[2][3][4]

items.title: Trump says Iran war could last four weeks as combat operations intensify

featured_image.name: Iran Strikes: Trump Says More US Casualties Likely as ...

items.description:
President Donald Trump declared on Sunday that U.S. military operations in Iran will continue "in full force" until all American objectives are met, as the joint U.S.-Israeli campaign entered its second day with mounting casualties on all sides and retaliatory strikes reverberating across the Middle East.[1][2]

In a video posted to Truth Social, Trump acknowledged the deaths of three American service members and warned that more losses are likely. "Combat operations continue at this time in full force, and they will continue until all of our objectives are achieved," he said, pledging to "avenge" the fallen troops. In a phone interview with the Daily Mail, Trump offered the clearest timeline yet for the campaign, saying, "It's always been a four-week process. We figured it will be four weeks or so. It's a big country. It'll take four weeks — or less".[2][3][4][1]

items.title: Major shipping firms halt Suez Canal transit after strikes on Iran

featured_image.name: Maersk tests Red Sea route as Gaza ceasefire offers hope ...

items.description:
A.P. Moller-Maersk announced on Sunday that it will halt all sailings through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and the Suez Canal, rerouting vessels around the Cape of Good Hope after U.S. and Israeli military strikes on Iran plunged the region's key maritime chokepoints into crisis. The decision reverses the Danish shipping giant's recent move to resume transit through the Red Sea corridor, which had been disrupted by Houthi rebel attacks since late 2023.[1][2]

"Due to the deteriorating security situation in the Middle East region following the escalating military conflict, we have decided to pause future Trans-Suez sailings through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait for the time being," Maersk said in a statement.[3][1]

items.title: Trump says he agreed to talk with Iran as strikes continue

featured_image.name: Trump said considering Iranian offer of indirect nuclear ...

items.description: The United States and Israel launched a massive joint military operation against Iran on February 28, killing Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and dozens of senior military and political leaders in what the Pentagon dubbed "Operation Epic Fury" and Israel codenamed "Roaring Lion." Iran responded with retaliatory missile and drone strikes across the Middle East, targeting Israel and U.S. military bases in at least six countries, killing three American service members and raising fears of a wider regional war.

items.title: ESA releases new images of interstellar comet ahead of Jupiter flyby

featured_image.name: Interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS caught on camera in new images ...

items.description:
The interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS, the third object ever confirmed to have entered our solar system from beyond, is heading for a close encounter with Jupiter on March 16, when it will pass within 33 million miles of the gas giant. The flyby marks one of the final observable milestones before the ancient visitor disappears into the void of interstellar space.[1][2][3]

First detected in July 2025 by a NASA-funded ATLAS telescope in Chile, the comet has captivated astronomers with its extraordinary speed — clocked at 137,000 miles per hour — and a hyperbolic trajectory confirming it could not have originated in our solar system. Only two interstellar objects had previously been identified: 1I/'Oumuamua in 2017 and 2I/Borisov in 2019.[4][5][6][7]

items.title: Iran's foreign minister vows 'no limit' to self-defense after Khamenei killed

featured_image.name: An interview with Iran's foreign minister

items.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi declared on Sunday that Iran sees "no limit" to its right to self-defense following the assassination of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in coordinated US-Israeli strikes, rejecting President Donald Trump's warnings against retaliation and framing the military response as a matter of national survival.

items.title: Death toll at Iranian girls' school rises to 148

featured_image.name: Death toll rises to 148 in US-Israel strike on Iranian girls ...

items.description:
A missile strike on a girls' elementary school in the southern Iranian city of Minab emerged as the deadliest single incident of the joint U.S.-Israeli military operation against Iran, with the death toll climbing from an initial count of 108 reported by the Iranian Red Crescent to 148 according to the local prosecutor, as cited by Iranian state media and confirmed by The Wall Street Journal and CNN.[1][2]

The strike hit the Shajareh Tayyebeh all-girls primary school at approximately 10:45 a.m. local time on Saturday, February 28, as roughly 170 students between the ages of seven and 12 were attending class during what is a regular school day in Iran. The impact destroyed the building's walls and caused its roof to collapse, burying students underneath the rubble. Verified footage showed thick black smoke rising from a structure adorned with pastel-painted flowers, as rescuers used cranes and shovels to reach those trapped inside.[3][4][5][6]

items.title: CIA tracked Khamenei for months before Israel struck Tehran

featured_image.name: Exclusive: Prior to Iran attacks, CIA assessed Khamenei ...

items.description:
The CIA monitored Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei's movements for months before identifying a rare gathering of Iran's top political and military leaders at a government compound in central Tehran on Saturday morning, providing the intelligence that enabled Israel to launch a precision strike killing Khamenei and more than 40 senior officials, according to reports from The New York Times citing people familiar with the operation.[1][2]

The agency passed what officials described as "high fidelity" intelligence on Khamenei's location to Israel, prompting U.S. and Israeli forces to accelerate the timing of a joint military campaign that had been weeks in planning. The breakthrough came when CIA sources learned that Khamenei would be present at the compound alongside senior security aides for a Saturday morning meeting, rather than the evening session originally expected.[3][4][5]

items.title: US calls Iran's claim it struck USS Lincoln a 'lie'

featured_image.name: USS Abraham Lincoln strike group nears Iran amid rising tensions

items.description:
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed on Sunday that it struck the aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln with four ballistic missiles in the Persian Gulf, a claim the US military swiftly and forcefully rejected as a "LIE."

The IRGC issued the claim as part of what Tehran calls Operation True Promise 4, a retaliatory campaign following joint US and Israeli strikes that killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. If confirmed, the strike would have marked the first direct hit on a US aircraft carrier in decades. But US Central Command left no room for ambiguity.

items.title: 3 US service members killed in Iran operation, CENTCOM says

featured_image.name: 3 American soldiers killed, 5 seriously injured in war with ...

items.description: US Central Command confirmed on the morning of March 1 that three American service members have been killed in action and five others seriously wounded during Operation Epic Fury, the ongoing joint US-Israeli military campaign against Iran. The deaths mark the first American combat fatalities since the operation began on February 28.

items.title: Brent crude surges to $80 as Iran conflict shuts Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: How could the U.S. strikes in Iran affect the world's oil supply?

items.description:
Brent crude surged roughly 10 percent to about $80 a barrel in off-market transactions on Sunday, as U.S. and Israeli military strikes on Iran threw global energy markets into turmoil and effectively shut down one of the world's most critical oil chokepoints.[1][2]

The spike came as shipping through the Strait of Hormuz — a narrow waterway responsible for more than 20 percent of global oil transit — ground to a halt after Iran's Revolutionary Guards contacted vessels to declare the strait closed. Iranian state television reported that an oil tanker attempting to pass through the strait was struck and was sinking, broadcasting footage of a burning vessel at sea.[3][4][5][6][7]
